_note: What shipped, newest first, one entry per update that went live. version/build/date/commit are read out of git rather than typed — the deploy stamps version.json as 1.0.<commit count>, so an entry's version is the release it actually shipped in and scripts/verify-updates.js checks every one of them against the history. The titles and lines are written by hand, for somebody who wants to know what changed rather than what the diff was.

updates.title: The run sheet
items: A new DM page: one screen to have open while running a session. Where you left off, the chapter's running order with how long each section should take, the side quests on offer, the current Heat and who turns up at it, and the encounter presets for the arc.
Plus a notes box that saves, because what you write at nine o'clock is what you need at the start of the next session.
Nothing on it is a second copy of anything — change the campaign, the session log, the Heat or the presets in their own place and this page follows.

updates.title: At the Table
items: A new player page showing the fight from your seat: whose turn it is, whether you are next, the order, everyone's conditions and a health bar — live, while the DM runs the encounter.
Enemy hit points show as a band rather than a number — Untouched, Grazed, Bloodied, Critical, Down. Your own side shows real numbers. The DM can toggle the rest on.
Where a condition changes an attack roll it says so for whoever is up now, and every condition carries its own rule as a tooltip.
The board shows where everybody is standing; this shows when.

updates.title: Your character in the Lab
items: The Lab opens on your own character now: everything you can do on one screen, grouped by whether it costs an action, a bonus action or a reaction — your quirk's abilities, the gear you carry that states a die, and the standard options every character has.
Every row with a die has a button that rolls it, and an arrow that opens it on the workbench.
Your seven abilities are a strip at the top — tap one to roll a d20 against it. It shows the natural roll as well as the total, because a 24 could be a natural 20 or a natural 16.
It shows the characters your DM has assigned you, the same ones you can edit in the Class 1-A toolkit. The DM sees the whole class.

updates.title: The Lab and the Heat track
items: Two new tabs for players. The Lab builds an ability and tells you what it actually does — the range, the average, how often it hits an AC you pick, and what it's worth per use once misses are counted.

The Lab's other half is a quirk database: every quirk in the campaign, from all seven places a character can be hiding, searchable and filterable. An ability with a damage expression can be opened straight on the workbench.

The Heat track shows how much attention Byakko are paying, who shows up at this level, and what is coming — the next band is named before you are standing in it, and from Heat 6 it warns about the Corners.
It also keeps the record: all twenty-one named Byakko by rank, who you have beaten, and a win-loss line per character. The Law is on it, with room for a seventh rule.
Everybody can read the Heat track; only the DM can move it.

updates.title: Loot, more than doubled
items: The loot tables go from 82 items to 194, and from eight tables to twelve.

Four new tables for the rooms that had none: the Ring at Swing Town (what you win in the back cage on a Friday), the Cage (one entry per floor of the climb), Kurogane Wharf (the gym, the Anchor and the docks), and the chop shop.
Byakko, all four Underground societies and the ordinary-things table are d20s now; the support lab is a d20 and the archive a d12.
A rail of every table at the top of the page, with the number of rows showing — during a search those become hit counts, so you can see which table the thing you typed is in.

updates.title: Party at a glance
items: A new DM page showing every character as one sortable table — level, HP, AC, speed, proficiency, quirk DC, passive score and all seven modifiers.
Under it, the low, average and high of every column, which is the row you actually want when setting a DC.
Tap any column to sort by it, tap again to reverse, tap a name for that character's printable sheet. Prints landscape.
The passive column is 10 + WIS with no proficiency added, because the character data records none — the page says so rather than quietly printing a number that's too low.
The printable sheet and the party table now share one loader, so they can never disagree about who's in the class or what someone's modifier is.

updates.title: Conditions that do something
items: The Encounter Manager now works out advantage and disadvantage from the conditions already on the row. Mark a target Restrained and the attack rolls with advantage, with the reason shown under the result.
One advantage and one disadvantage cancel, and the log says so instead of looking like a plain roll.
An attacker who is stunned, paralyzed or unconscious gets "no attack" with the reason, rather than a roll it should never have made.
Dropping to 0 HP now applies Unconscious, and healing takes it back off — unless you applied it yourself, in which case it stays.
Fixed: initiative was capped at 20, so a high-DEX character rolling well was squashed into a tie. It is d20 + DEX now, uncapped.
Fixed: the Unconscious entry in the rules reference never said attacks against it have advantage — only that melee hits crit.
The DM's quick roller gained advantage and disadvantage, and every die in the Encounter Manager now rolls through the shared engine.

updates.title: Dice and paper
items: One dice engine behind every roller on the site. The notation now reads d20, 2d6+3, several terms at once like 2d6+1d4+3, "d20 adv" or "dis" for advantage, and 4d6kh3 to keep the highest three.
Dropped dice are shown struck through rather than hidden, so you can always see what the other die said.
The Heropad's Dice app gained advantage, disadvantage, critical hits and an expression box — it had none of them before.

A printable character sheet: one character to a page, black on white, with your scores, saves, quirk abilities, what you're carrying and lines to write on. Reads your live character, and says on the paper if it had to fall back to the bundled copy.

updates.title: Rules reference
items: A new Rules page, open to everyone: 106 rules across ten sections — the d20, your turn, moving, cover, areas of effect, damage, death saves, conditions, resting, and how this toolkit handles the fiddly bits.
One search box across the lot, with the words you typed marked in the hits. Press / to search from anywhere on the page.
A Rules app on the Heropad, so the answer is in your pocket rather than on the DM's screen.
The conditions and cover reference in the Encounter Manager now reads the same file, so the DM's copy and the players' copy cannot drift apart.

updates.title: Loot tables
items: Eight rollable tables of unique items behind the DM block: Byakko street trophies, the four Underground societies, the support lab, Appetite and Clean Read, and ordinary things worth more than they look.
Eighty-two items, each hanging off something already written — the hook on every row says what.
Underground items stay off the shop page, which is what keeps the Underground hidden, and the checks enforce it.

updates.title: A Friday night at the Ring
items: Swing Town's fight club in detail: two tables — who is on the card, banded by Heat, and what else is in the room.
All thirty-two rows end in where they lead, and every one points at something already in the campaign: Clean Read, the Scarlet Legion, the white van, the seventh rule.

updates.title: The notes on the players' phone
items: The Heropad has an Updates app, so the players see what changed too — the dashboard header is a thing only the DM looks at.
An unread dot on the dashboard's version badge, driven by the notes being written rather than by a deploy.
scripts/add-update.js adds the next entry without anybody hand-computing a version out of git.

updates.title: Run the ladder
items: An encounter group that sits on a running order now shows the whole arc: which step you are on, what is in it, and one button that adds the line-up and loads its map.
Where your table has got to is remembered in your browser, not written into the shared encounter document.

updates.title: After Hours — The Story, Short
items: A seventh campaign in the library that is a summary of the first one: eight chapters, one page each, what happens and what turns.
For getting a grip on the story without reading thirty sessions of material. Nothing in it is new, and it says so — where it and the full module disagree, the module is right.

updates.title: What's New
items: A page listing everything added to the toolkit, update by update, newest first — and this is the entry where it started.
Each entry's version, build, date and commit are read out of git rather than typed, so an entry cannot claim a release that never shipped.
The version badge in the dashboard header is a link to it now.

updates.title: Search every module at once
items: The Campaigns library has a search box that runs over every module at once, so you don't have to know which one holds the answer.
Each result says which module it came from, and clicking it opens that module and flashes the paragraph it sent you to.
Press / to jump to the search box from anywhere on the page.

updates.title: Kurogane Wharf
items: Nakata's gym, the Anchor café and the docks after midnight, written up as one place with three uses — and the Legion underneath it after dark.
A preset map for Nakata's Gym, and a "Thralls on the wharf" encounter group pointed at the container yard.
The Legion's discovery ladder now names the group its witness rung is built on.

updates.title: The chop shop
items: Kōno Sae's lock-up written up: vans, plates, no questions, and the counter a man with a scar bled on.
The only disruption in the turf economy with no sting in it, now said plainly — and what it costs when the class take it.
A preset map, and a chop shop encounter group at step six of the Byakko ladder, which had been loading Madame Tsuru's group by mistake.
Madame Tsuru's group moved to her real room, Lucky Seven, on the noodle bar's own map.

updates.title: Every live campaign has a local copy
items: "Robs handwritten" existed only on the live Firestore document. It is in the repo now, verified field for field against live.

updates.title: The noodle bar, and Lucky Seven above it
items: Rule four's building, which turned out to be two: the only neutral ground in the backstreets, and Madame Tsuru's dice den directly above it.
Lucky Seven's game written out so a player can sit down at it — 2d6 against the house, ties to the house, ¥100 off every pot.
Preset maps can now carry elevation and labels, so a two-floor building is one map with the stairwell between the floors.

updates.title: Swing Town, and Byakko in daylight
items: Swing Town written up room by room — the cages, the chalk wall, the vending wall, the back cage and the office — and it reads as the Heat barometer.
A d20 of things the gang is doing in public where anybody can see, none of them a fight.
The backstreets week: what is on Monday through Sunday, so "what's happening tonight?" has the same answer every time.
A preset map for Swing Town, which Friday's Ring fight now loads instead of the festival arena.

updates.title: Fog that hides what it is hiding
items: Fog hid the drawing and nothing else: hovering a hidden token named it, the cursor gave its position away, and clicking it drew a glow on an empty-looking square. Fixed.
The players' phone shows the richer session log — the chapter, who was there, who they met, where they went — and deliberately never the DM's "next time" note.

updates.title: Search inside a module, and where you left off
items: A search box inside an open campaign that indexes every authored field, including read-alouds, and jumps to the block.
The dashboard shows the last session you logged and its "next time" line, in the DM view only.

updates.title: A straight line through Byakko
items: Nine steps from the kid on the crash barrier to the roof of the Cage, for tables that want the backstreets to be a story rather than a weather system.
Each step names the encounter preset to load and where to set Heat; the sandbox is still the default and the section says so.

updates.title: A session log worth keeping
items: Sessions now record the chapter, who was at the table, the NPCs met and the places visited, plus a "next time" line.
Attendance is ticked from the roster and counted per player above the list; search runs across every field.
The encounter page gained a Rules button: what all fourteen conditions actually do, plus the cover scale, with the same lines as tooltips on every condition chip.

updates.title: Big creatures, doors that shut, and undo
items: Tokens can be 1×1 to 4×4. Kuma arrives at 2×2, because his own stat block says 9'5" at rest.
Doors can be shut, and a shut door is a wall — so it blocks line of sight too.
A sight radius for dark corridors, condition pips on tokens, undo on Ctrl+Z, and the board exportable as an image.

updates.title: Line of sight on a switch
items: One checkbox hides every square the players' own characters cannot see, and keeps up as they move. Walls block sight; cover does not.
A colour brush for painting squares any colour, with no rules attached.
The board's twenty-odd controls regrouped into three readable rows, and the combatant list reads as cards.

updates.title: Nine more maps and five new board layers
items: Hospital, classroom block, apartments, night market, half-built high-rise, subway, holding wing, bathhouse and mountain road.
Fog of war, square labels, elevation, area shapes (burst, cone, line) and saved maps you build yourself.
Twenty encounter groups — a whole line-up in one click, with the map it was written for.

updates.title: Eight big preset maps
items: Maps two to three times the old size: Hosu District, U.A. campus, the mall, an expressway overpass, a factory, the docks, station platforms and an underground hideout.
Fourteen new prefabs to furnish them.
Festival Arena's four gates never actually opened — its wall ring is two squares thick and the doors only cut one layer. Fixed.

updates.title: Byakko and the Underground in folders
items: The street gang and the three societies filed one folder per faction on the Characters tab.

updates.title: Scenery on the battle board
items: Twenty-nine prefabs — buildings, trees, vehicles, scatter — and ten preset battlefields.
Auto-terrain marks the squares a prop covers, and takes it back when the prop moves.
Duplicate combatant ids are repaired rather than reverting your edits, and a failed board save says so instead of silently undoing itself.

updates.title: A second season, and a readable campaign
items: Chapters 7 and 8 of After Hours, the Ledger as a fourth Underground faction, and Byakko's middle ranks, Heat events and turf economy.
The campaign reader rebuilt around the fact that campaign text is plain text: bullets, small-caps lead-ins and read-aloud cue cards instead of one wall of line breaks.
All fifty-seven read-alouds rewritten to be said rather than read.

updates.title: The gang on the Characters tab
items: Thirty Byakko and Underground stat blocks existed in the encounter builder and nowhere else. They are on the Characters tab now.

updates.title: Supporting NPCs filed properly
items: The thirteen supporting NPCs moved out of one "AI made" folder into category folders.

updates.title: The Shortlist: After Hours
items: A new campaign alongside The Shortlist rather than over it, rewritten for the cast as the live sheets have them.
The Byakko street gang with its Heat track, three Underground societies, and new shop stock for students who are not allowed to hurt anybody.

updates.title: Adding a combatant stopped eating another
items: The id counter restarted on every page load, so a newly added character could be handed an id the server was already using, and a row would vanish a moment later.

updates.title: Editable kit, and encounter fixes
items: Players can edit their own item rows.
The encounter page's sort and End Turn behaviour fixed.

updates.title: Inventory on a phone
items: Players keep their own kit, and the bottom of the Inventory tab is reachable on a short phone screen.

updates.title: The Shortlist's opening chapter
items: Kinji Hamakida, the opening chapter, and the encounter presets to run it.

updates.title: Kinji Hamakida
items: Smeet Nozoto renamed to Kinji Hamakida across all 122 references, including the older "Kinosho Kochimiko" fossil name still in campaign prose.

updates.title: Typing in missing ability scores
items: A character built field by field through the page had no ability scores, so the stat boxes looked editable and were not. They are now.

updates.title: Relationship categories
items: People get a category instead of a true/false "is this a PC", so teachers, villains and rival classes have somewhere to be — and the sidebar can close the ones you are not using.

updates.title: The Shortlist filled out
items: Stat blocks for Sylar, Riddle, Powder, Touch Up and Kuma, a session map onto the sixteen to eighteen it claims, levelling guidance, and the nineteen classmates a DM has to voice.
Class 1-A's twentieth student.
